messages:
olivia: quick flag  the API ref for /v1/search shows query param `limit` as a string in the curl example (`?limit=\"10\"`) and in the OpenAPI example YAML. our server accepts integer only and the Go SDK typed it as int, so users copying the string example get `400` or a type error.

harry: thanks, that explains a support case. is it just the examples or the parameter schema too?

olivia: both in a couple places. openapi/paths/search.yaml has `schema: type: string` for limit (probably copied from an earlier draft), and the generated curl/py snippets use `limit: \"10\"`.

harry: I'll take this. plan: update the OpenAPI schema to `type: integer, format: int32`, update all examples to use `?limit=10`, fix SDK snippet examples in docs (python/js/go), and add a short note in the param description: \"integer; pass numeric value without quotes\".

olivia: can you also add a migration note? some users might have pasted quoted numbers from the docs and pinned behavior. a one-line in the migration guide is fine.

harry: added migration note: \"limit must be a number; remove surrounding quotes.\" and added a changelog bullet for the docs correction.

ci-bot: docs-ci started for PR 4589 (:building_construction:)

harry: I ran the docs example lint/validator locally and added a unit in tools/docs/validate_examples to parse querystring values against the OpenAPI param types so we catch this going forward.

support-bot: support ticket #20241 linked: user used `?limit=\"5\"` and received 400; resolved by pointing to updated docs.

ci-bot: docs-ci passed for PR 4589 (:white_check_mark:) https://ci.internal.redwood/4589

olivia: LGTM. can we also search the repo for `limit=\"` and `limit='` patterns to be safe? there were a few localized cheatsheets that might have this.

harry: good idea. I ran repo search and fixed two more occurrences in internal quickstart snippets. pushed branch and merged, cherry-picked into `stable/docs` for the backport.

olivia: thanks! this should cut down on the small but noisy 400s.

harry: np. small docs bug, big customer happiness :)
